owner_decisions: [LAUNCH] The Quit item's label and shortcut come from AppKit and appear nowhere in source; any Windows Exit affordance is an addition. :: Owner must choose the label and chord of the Windows quit affordance. Source confirms the gap: App/AppCommands.swift:11-104 replaces .appSettings (:12), .saveItem (:19), .newItem (:27), .help (:101), inserts before .windowArrangement (:21) and after .sidebar (:37), and adds CommandMenu("Thread") (:55). It never touches .appTermination, so no quit string and no quit chord exist in the pinned tree. What must be chosen, exactly: (a) the visible label (for example "Exit" per Windows convention versus "Quit Marrow" per the source's framework wording), and (b) whether it carries Alt+F4 only, or also a menu chord. Neither is derivable, and both are visible on first use.

[LAUNCH] The app deliberately survives with no visible window; a Windows app with no window and no tray icon is unreachable. :: Owner must choose between two named deviations; source confirms the trap but offers no exit. SOURCE FACT: App/AppDelegate.swift has no applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed, and :30-33 exists specifically to bring the window back on reopen; App/Window/WindowManager.swift:98 sets `window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false` and :27-28 caches and reuses the same NSWindow, so closing it destroys nothing. A whole-tree grep for NSStatusItem and NSStatusBar returns nothing: there is no tray affordance in source. The only in-app way back is App/AppCommands.swift:21-25, a Window-menu item titled AppInfo.name bound to the .showMainWindow chord (default Command-0, Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:233), and on Windows a menu bar does not survive its window. Owner must pick exactly one: (a) the close button exits the process, or (b) close hides the window and a notification-area icon reopens it. Both are departures and both are visible on the first window close.

[WIN] Caption buttons: source pins close/minimize/zoom to the LEADING edge; keep them there on Windows or mirror to the trailing edge? :: Owner must rule; source states the parity values and nothing else. SOURCE FACT, verified: UI/Chrome/WindowChrome.swift:177-199 constrains each of [.closeButton, .miniaturizeButton, .zoomButton] to `titlebar.leadingAnchor` at `leading + index * Chrome.trafficLightPitch`, with leading = Chrome.trafficLightLeading (18) and top = Chrome.trafficLightTop (16) when the sidebar is visible, and leading = Chrome.sheetInset + Chrome.chromeHorizontalPadding (0 + 14 = 14) and top = collapsedTrafficLightTop (:136-138 = 0 + 12 + (32-14)/2 = 21) when it is hidden. Pitch is 14 + 9 = 23 and diameter is 14 (Chrome.swift:15-21, :31-38). Exactly what must be chosen: keep app-drawn caption controls on the LEFT of the Windows window at (18,16)/(14,21) as source pins them, or mirror the whole group to the trailing edge, which changes six specified geometry values and their anchor. If mirroring is chosen it must be recorded as a named accepted deviation in the form of UNK-0004, never labelled parity. Needs its own UNK id; none exists yet.

[WIN] Chord notation: KeyChord.description renders macOS glyphs, and a refusal string names three of them verbatim. :: Owner must rule; verbatim-string parity and platform-idiomatic notation genuinely conflict here. SOURCE FACT: Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:43-50 `modifierSymbols` concatenates "⌃" (control), "⌥" (option), "⇧" (shift), "⌘" (command) in that fixed order with NO separator, and :32-34 `description` is that prefix plus KeyNames.label(for:). :326 is the refusal `"Add ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ so typing still works."`. These strings reach the user in at least three places: the Shortcuts settings rows, ShortcutStore.label(for:) (:288-290) and ShortcutStore.hint(for:) (:295-298), which composes help text like "Hide terminal (⌘J)". Exactly what must be chosen: (a) reproduce the glyphs and the no-separator concatenation byte for byte, or (b) render Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Win notation and reword the refusal to name Ctrl/Alt/Win. Option (b) changes user-visible strings that port_impacts.md entry 110 (CC1) says to carry verbatim, so it is an owner-approved deviation, not an engineering choice.

[WIN] The reserved-chord refusal names the other platform: 'macOS or Droppy Code already uses this chord.' :: Same class as the item above; owner must rule. SOURCE FACT: Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:329 is exactly `if Self.reserved.contains(chord) { return "macOS or Droppy Code already uses this chord." }`, and the reserved table at :252-257 is 18 chords: key codes [12,4,46,8,9,7,0,6] with Command, then code 6 with Shift+Command, then [18,19,20,21,23,22,26,28,25] with Command. Code 4 is H and code 46 is M (:53-56), so Command-H (Hide) and Command-M (Minimize) are reserved for macOS system behavior that does not exist on Windows. Exactly what must be chosen: (a) keep the 18-entry table and the sentence verbatim, accepting that a Windows user is told macOS uses a chord, (b) keep the table and reword the sentence, or (c) drop the two macOS-only entries, which would let a Windows user bind a chord upstream refuses. [UPDATE] [UPDATE] Q162: two macOS security gates (Developer ID team pin + spctl Gatekeeper) collapse into one Authenticode check; whether to pin a publisher certificate thumbprint is undecided and no Windows signing identity exists. :: CONCRETE HARM, and it is sharper than the agent stated. [LAUNCH] The source contributes no single-instance lock; macOS gets that behavior from Launch Services. [LAUNCH] The 4 minute quit deferral cannot be honoured under a Windows logoff or shutdown. :: DECIDED: reproduce the deferral exactly on the ordinary quit path, and request the OS grace on session end without claiming it. [LAUNCH] SwitchLatency is shipped, non-#if-guarded code that is inert outside the dev bundle id; is the dev instrumentation kept? :: DECIDED: do not port it; replace the requirement with a recorded no-op. [WIN] The defaults key holding the main window frame is an AppKit convention, not a source fact; only the autosave NAME is in source. :: DECIDED: the port defines its own key; nothing migrates. SOURCE FACT: App/Window/WindowManager.swift:24 is the whole of it, `private static let mainFrameName = "DroppyCodeMainWindow"`, used at :67 `setFrameUsingName` and :70 `setFrameAutosaveName`; the defaults key AppKit derives from it is not in the tree. The user-visible contract IS in source and is what must be reproduced: on first run with no stored frame, the window opens at 1320x860 (:19) centered (:68); thereafter it restores its saved frame; the content minimum is 860x560 (:20, :66). [WIN] fitTitlebar and the titlebar frameDidChange observer reach into AppKit's private titlebar hierarchy; there is no Windows view to fit. :: DECIDED: implement the OUTCOME as a constant-height caption band and drop the AppKit plumbing. SOURCE FACT: the observable purpose is stated in the source's own words at UI/Chrome/WindowChrome.swift:140-147 - AppKit hands a click or hover to a caption button only inside the title bar's own bounds, its bar stops short of buttons levelled with the chrome, and the clicks fell through. fitTitlebar (:161-172) therefore grows the container to `titlebarHeight` keeping its top edge, where titlebarHeight = Chrome.sheetInset + Chrome.chromeTopPadding + Chrome.capsuleHeight = 0 + 12 + 32 = 44 (:148-150 with Chrome.swift:11, :32, :33-34, :38). DECISION: on Windows the WM_NCHITTEST caption band is a fixed 44 device-independent pixels from the window's top edge, recomputed on resize and on DPI change; every chrome control keeps a NoWindowDragArea equivalent so a press on a control never drags the window (:145-147). The private-hierarchy probe (:153-155), the frameDidChange observer (:62-66, :77-87) and its one-queued-fit coalescing (:80-84) do NOT port: they exist only because AppKit re-tiles the bar, which Windows does not do. Preserve the one part that IS observable: the unanimated re-place after a live resize ends (:91-95). No product visibility; re-examine only if the chosen stack draws its own non-client area differently.

[SIDEBAR] The reorder alignment haptic has no Windows desktop equivalent; does the owner want a substitute cue? :: DECIDED: omit it, add nothing. SOURCE FACT: App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:799 is the single site, `NSHapticFeedbackManager.defaultPerformer.perform(.alignment, performanceTime: .now)`, fired once per accepted swap. [SIDEBAR] Search uses Swift lowercased() and the picker uses localizedCaseInsensitiveContains; does a Windows ordinal-ignore-case comparison agree? :: DECIDED: they are two different comparisons and must be implemented as two different comparisons; ordinal-ignore-case is wrong for both. SOURCE FACT: the sidebar search folds with `lowercased()` then `contains` - query at App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:739, project name at :742, thread titles at :744 against the cache built at :2653. Swift's `lowercased()` is Unicode FULL, locale-INDEPENDENT default case conversion, which can change string length. The picker path uses `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains`, which is locale-SENSITIVE. DECISIONS: (1) implement `lowercased()` as Unicode Default Case Conversion with no locale tailoring - in a JS/TS stack that is exactly `String.prototype.toLowerCase()`; never ordinal case folding, never a locale-tailored ToLower, because Turkish dotless-i tailoring and simple-vs-full mapping of U+0130 both diverge from Swift; (2) implement `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains` as a locale-sensitive collator search at secondary strength in the user's current locale - in a JS/TS stack `Intl.Collator(undefined, {usage:'search', sensitivity:'accent'})`; (3) add the pinning fixture both requirements already call for, covering at minimum U+0130, U+0131, the final sigma pair, and a combining-mark case, and assert the two comparisons disagree where the source makes them disagree. Not a product choice: the user-visible contract is 'matches the same strings the source matches', and these are the implementations that satisfy it.

[SIDEBAR] The scroll freeze lifts immediately on an .idle scroll phase, but WM_MOUSEWHEEL has no scroll-end signal. :: DECIDED: the 150 ms debounce is the sole governor for wheel input; wire a scroll-end to the immediate lift only where the input stack actually reports one. SOURCE FACT: the freeze's only effect is `.allowsHitTesting(!isListScrolling)` on the list (App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:115). It is raised by noteListScroll() (:391-403), which sets the flag once per scroll and re-arms a 150 ms settle task on every movement (:397-402), and it is lifted either by that task or immediately by `.onScrollPhaseChange` when phase == .idle, which also cancels the task (:140-143). DECISION: on Windows, a raw wheel scroll lifts the freeze 150 ms after the last tick, exactly the debounce the source already runs for a scroll that has not reported idle; where the stack does surface a terminal scroll phase (precision touchpad through Direct Manipulation, or a pointer-event sequence with a terminal phase), route it to the immediate lift so that path matches the source exactly. Worst observable difference: up to 150 ms of ignored clicks after the last wheel tick, on wheel input only. Record in COMPATIBILITY.

[SIDEBAR] Chrome.glideSpring's settlingDuration drives the glide's handover; will a Windows spring solver compute the same value for response 0.6 / damping 0.86? :: DECIDED: derive the handover from the solver's own settle time, never hardcode a macOS-measured constant. SOURCE FACT: UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:106 is `Spring(response: 0.6, dampingRatio: 0.86)`; App/Views/Sidebar/RowGlide.swift:18 aliases it, :225 drives the keyframes with it, and :228-236 is the whole contract - sleep for `max(spring.settlingDuration - 0.12, 0)`, then arrive(), then sleep 0.12, then finish(). The comments at :114-115 and :229-230 state the intent plainly: the real row comes back under the ghost's last frames so the handover never shows a gap, and the ghost goes once the keyframes have run their course. DECISION: (1) implement the spring with the same parameterisation, angular frequency omega0 = 2*pi/response = 10.472 rad/s and zeta = 0.86; (2) define settlingDuration analytically as the time the envelope decays to 1/1000 of the initial displacement, ln(1000)/(zeta*omega0), approximately 0.767 s for these values, and pin that in a unit test; (3) compute the 0.12 s handover FROM that value at runtime, so if the solver's settle time is ever retuned the ghost is still removed after the animation visually ends and never before. The failure the source is guarding against is a visible gap or a ghost outliving its motion; both are avoided by the derivation, not by matching Apple's number. AttachmentFlight.swift:102 uses the same property and takes the same treatment.

[CHAT] The drift, blank-repair, viewport-nudge and stack-generation machinery exists to correct a virtualized list built against a remembered viewport; is any of it needed on Windows? :: DECIDED: the timeline list derives its visible range from the LIVE scroll offset every frame, and these four are then recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_EVIDENCE rather than implemented. Justification: all four exist only to correct an artefact of SwiftUI's lazy stack building rows against a remembered viewport - PR-CHAT-056 tells the lazy list where the viewport is once accumulated drift passes a tolerance, PR-CHAT-167 rebuilds the list from scratch by bumping a generation identity. None of them is a product behavior a user asked for; the user-visible contract is 'the rows on screen are the rows at the current scroll offset, and none is blank'. A list whose visible range is computed from the live offset satisfies that contract directly and makes the corrections dead by construction. REQUIRED FORM OF THE RECORD, so this is not a quiet drop: each of the four keeps its requirement, states the tolerance, the nudge and the generation bump as specified from source, and carries an explicit note naming the design property that makes it a no-op. If the chosen stack turns out to virtualize against a remembered viewport after all, the four become live and must be implemented as specified. No product visibility either way.

[PROVCLI] Q57 [PROVCLI] The shipped Command Code mod's orphan test is `process.ppid === 1`, a POSIX idiom with no Windows meaning; a stranded gate waits the full six hours. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at CommandCodeAPI.swift:428-431: `if (process.ppid === 1 || Date.now() - started > 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000) { try { fs.unlinkSync(request) } catch {}; return {block: true, additionalContext: 'Droppy Code did not answer.'} }`. [PROVCLI] Q63 [PROVCLI] Copilot de-duplicates reasoning text by Swift hashValue, which is randomly seeded per process; the port must not turn it into a persisted key. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at CopilotSession.swift:1068: `text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).hashValue`. [PROVACP] Q68 [PROVACP] StdioProcess.terminate's three-second graceful window has no Windows equivalent: TerminateProcess behaves like SIGKILL, so the first step is already forceful and the second redundant. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at StdioProcess.swift:114-122: stdin is closed on the write queue FIRST, then `process.terminate()` (SIGTERM), then SIGKILL at +3 seconds if still running. [PROVREG] Q84 [PROVREG] LoginEnvironment.which splits PATH on colon and tests the POSIX execute bit; Windows needs semicolon splitting and PATHEXT, and `cmd` resolves to the system interpreter. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at Shell.swift:411-423: if the name contains '/', expand the tilde and accept it when `isExecutableFile`; otherwise take `environment["PATH"] ?? augmentedPath(nil)`, split on ':', append the name to each directory, and return the first that is an executable file, else nil. [PROVREG] Q89 [PROVREG] Command-cache keys are rawValue + newline + directory path, compared as exact strings; on Windows one directory has several spellings, giving two cache entries and two CLI launches. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at ProviderRegistry.swift:676-678: `static func commandKey(_ provider: ProviderKind, directory: String) -> String { provider.rawValue + "\n" + directory }`, used at :681 with an LRU eviction at 32 entries (:682-686). [PROVREG] Q90 [PROVREG] UsageLimitSignal.resetTime honours a parenthesised IANA zone identifier; Windows does not use IANA zone names natively and the source gives no mapping. :: SOURCE FACT, verified at UsageLimitSignal.swift:32-35: the regex `\(([A-Za-z_]+/[A-Za-z_]+)\)` is matched anywhere in the message, the parentheses are trimmed with `CharacterSet(charactersIn: "()")`, and `TimeZone(identifier:)` is applied; on either failure the `if let` simply falls through and `Calendar.current`'s own zone is used for `nextDate(after:matching:matchingPolicy:.nextTime)`. Validate the identifier and, when it is not recognized, do exactly what the source does - ignore the zone and fall through to the local zone - so an unmappable name degrades identically on both platforms. Do not build a Windows-zone translation table and do not error: the source's own failure path is the specification. Keep the regex, the trim set and the matchingPolicy verbatim.

[HYDRA] Q95 [HYDRA] The worktree folder slug replaces spaces only; Windows forbids characters macOS allows, and writer and sweeper must agree. :: DECIDED. Source is AppModel+Hydra.swift:492-495 (writer: `project.name.replacingOccurrences(of: " ", with: "-").lowercased()`, folder = "<slug>-<persona>-<8 hex>") and :1033-1043 (sweeper: longest slug that `name.hasPrefix(slug + "-")`, then the tail must split on "-" into <persona>[-<round>]-<8 hex>). Decision: add one shared function `hydraSlug(_:)` used at BOTH sites and nowhere else. It performs, in order: (1) replace U+0020 with "-", (2) lowercase, (3) replace each of < > : " / \ | ? * and every character U+0000-U+001F with "-". Nothing else. Justification against the contract: step 3 is the minimum Windows requires and is invisible to the user for every project name macOS and Windows both accept, so parity is exact on the whole overlapping domain. Mapping to "-" rather than deleting is safe because the sweeper strips the slug by prefix length before it counts hyphen-separated parts, so extra hyphens inside the slug cannot change the parts arithmetic. No trailing-dot or reserved-device-name handling is needed: the folder name is always "<slug>-<persona>-<8 hex>", so the slug is never the last component and never stands alone. Collision risk is unchanged from macOS (which already collides on case) and the sweeper's longest-slug rule already handles it.

[HYDRA] Q96 [HYDRA] hydraProject tests absoluteness with hasPrefix("/") and walks up to "/"; tilde expansion has no analogue. :: DECIDED, and port_impacts.md:172 entry 82 already records the shape. Decision, applied identically here and at every site in Q100/Q104/Q122: a path is ABSOLUTE if it matches /^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/ (drive-rooted), or /^\\\\[^\\/]+[\\/][^\\/]+/ (UNC \\server\share), or begins \\?\ . A bare leading "\" is NOT treated as absolute; it is joined onto the root, which preserves the source's behaviour of never silently escaping the checkout. The upward walk terminates when deletingLastPathComponent stops shortening the path, i.e. at "C:\" or "\\server\share", replacing `if dir == "/"`. Tilde: expand a leading "~" that is the whole string or is followed by \ or / to %USERPROFILE%; leave any other "~name" form unexpanded - which matches what NSString.expandingTildeInPath already does on a machine where that user does not exist, so it is the faithful degraded path, not an invention. No product surface changes: the user still types a project name or a path and the same project is resolved.

[TERM] Q126 [TERM] foregroundJobIsTheShell reads kp_eproc.e_tpgid against e_pgid via sysctl; ConPTY exposes neither. :: DECIDED. Its one caller is TerminalPanel.swift:339-346: a local keyDown monitor that, for keyCode 53 with no allowed modifiers and the terminal view as first responder, calls onEscapeAtPrompt() and SWALLOWS the event (return nil) only when the shell owns the foreground; otherwise it returns the event and Escape reaches the terminal. On each Escape, enumerate live descendants of the ConPTY child PID (a snapshot of the process tree, or the shell's Job Object accounting if the shell is launched in one) and return true when the shell has no live descendant. [TERM] Q127 [TERM] Two deliberately different termination ladders, neither of which Windows can express in signals. :: DECIDED, and the difference is preserved. Source verified: Shell.terminate (Shell.swift:110-118) - guard isRunning, process.terminate() [SIGTERM to the child], then 1 second later on a utility queue `kill(getpgid(pid) == pid ? -pid : pid, SIGKILL)`, i.e. the whole process GROUP when the child leads one, else the single pid. StdioProcess.terminate (StdioProcess.swift:115-123) - close the stdin write handle FIRST, guard isRunning, process.terminate(), then 3 seconds later `kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)`, single PID only, no group. Decision: (a) Shell - spawn each child in its own Job Object; graceful step = CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to the child's process group (spawned with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP), which is the only signal Windows can deliver to a console child and the nearest analogue of SIGTERM; after 1 second, TerminateJobObject, which kills the tree and is the faithful expression of the -pid group kill. (b) StdioProcess - close stdin first, unchanged; graceful step = CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to that child only; after 3 seconds, TerminateProcess on that PID alone, with NO job object, so grandchildren survive exactly as they do on macOS. The 1-second and 3-second deadlines, the stdin-close-first ordering, and the tree-vs-single-process scope are all preserved, so the two ladders stay distinguishable as triage_summary.json:92 requires. Record in COMPATIBILITY that the graceful step is CTRL_BREAK rather than SIGTERM and that a CLI ignoring CTRL_BREAK reaches the kill step where a macOS one would have exited.

[STORE] [STORE] Q171: Storage.root's Application Support analogue - %APPDATA% (Roaming) as specified, or %LOCALAPPDATA% which the Marrow build already uses. :: DECIDED: %LOCALAPPDATA%\<display name>. Two independent reasons, and they agree. (1) Compatibility, which is decisive on its own: the port already ships there. The owner runs 0.2.1 with data in %LOCALAPPDATA%, and the first start of a build from this branch takes over %LOCALAPPDATA%\Agent Workbench and becomes %LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow. Moving the root to %APPDATA% now would orphan every existing user's library, threads and attachments behind an app that no longer looks there - the exact harm PR-STORE-013 escalates, arrived at deliberately. (2) Semantics: ~/Library/Application Support is explicitly excluded from macOS's roaming and cloud sync, so its true Windows counterpart for a store of this shape - library.json, per-thread JSON, attachment blobs, wallpaper - is the local, non-roaming folder. %APPDATA% would push that volume through domain profile sync. The pinned source cannot decide this (Storage.swift:20-23 just asks Foundation for .applicationSupportDirectory), so it is mine, and it is recorded in the ADR. One thing the question missed and the ADR must also record: Storage has a SECOND root. Storage.swift:43-48 (stateDirectory) puts worktrees (:38) and patches (:41) under LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory + AppInfo.stateDirectoryName, i.e. the '.droppy-code' dotfolder in the user's HOME (Text.swift:6), not in Application Support. That one maps to %USERPROFILE%\<dot name> and must not be folded into %LOCALAPPDATA%, or git worktree paths change shape.
